doc.title: Wendy Oxenhorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 22, 2026

title: Assembling the concert after 9/11
summary: George Wein's Festival Productions lent producers, Bill Cosby signed on, and the first concert packed the house and raised 350 thousand dollars despite 9/11.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: was like this is incredible. “I’m going to give you my top producer.” And he gave us Rick White which was amazing, and Dan Melnick. And then some of the guys on our board, Bob Cranshaw and Jimmy Owens, they started reaching out to musicians. At the time I asked if anyone knew anyone famous. Someone had the number for Bill Cosby’s agent, so I left word. I remember a week later I get a call and I hear this guy with this voice that sounds familiar go, “Wendy?” I was like, “Yes.” He goes, “This is Cos.” Okay. This is before anyone knew what he was up to in his spare time. But to us in that time he was a big star yet, the Cosby show, that was like an A list name that was like Whoopi Goldberg to us, you know. So we got Cos, he said he’d do it and it just started snowballing. And we had only nine weeks to put it together. I told the board I have to hire someone because I cannot continue to do this alone. I was doing the emergencies, I was doing the bookkeeping, which I was terrible. I was raising the money, I was starting to recruit a board, I was doing the events, I was doing the marketing. It was insane. So they told me we could get an intern. So I contacted a friend of mine and he was teaching African studies in – oh I forgot the university, Adam Gusso, but he was an amazing guy. He also played harmonica with an all-blues band. And he sent one of his students who turned out to be the most brilliant young woman. She looked like she could be a little church girl from Atlanta. And it turned out she ended up leaving us to become an attorney. She got a full ride to Northeastern. She was just incredible. Lauren Roberts. And the two of us in nine weeks put this together. And 13 days before our first Great Night in Harlem we had – oh I think it was over a hundred of the living legends at the time coming together. Freddie Hubbard, I mean everyone. And 9/11 happened 13 days before. So we thought okay no one’s going to show. The house was packed. We had a four hour concert and we raised $350,000.
